mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months compresses discount rates for equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors shift to risk assets.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines for three consecutive months, or Rank IC falls below 0.02 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 4.5% for two consecutive months, it signals a weakening labor market that reduces consumer spending confidence, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 4.5% for two consecutive months, or Rank IC remains below 0.02 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates broad-based consumer demand contraction, triggering negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days as earnings expectations fall.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS decline for two consecutive months, or interaction term Rank IC falls below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS rising above 4.5% for three months), higher discount rates and reduced liquidity cause negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods during monetary tightening cycles, or regime-conditional Rank IC remains below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) over three consecutive months signals strong labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when PAYEMS increases for three consecutive months, or Rank IC falls below 0.02 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) fall below 1300.0 thousand units for two consecutive months, it indicates housing sector contraction that reduces overall consumer demand, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when HOUST falls below 1300.0 for two consecutive months, or Rank IC remains below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and quarterly GDP growth (GDPC1) indicates broad-based supply shock that reduces corporate profitability, triggering negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when both INDPRO and GDPC1 decline for two consecutive periods, or interaction term Rank IC falls below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: During late-cycle supply shocks (characterized by declining INDPRO and rising input costs), stagflationary pressures reduce corporate margins, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods during late-cycle supply shocks, or regime-conditional Rank IC remains below 0.02.
